dna.default: drive=constant, chain=triple - constant makes _drive_acceleration() hand the grabbed arrow straight back, so the shipped line ball.apply_central_force(accel * mass * SCENE_SCALE) is byte-identical, and the launch helper returns before touching velocity or gravity_scale (the ball still starts at rest under world gravity); triple only re-asserts visible = true on the three arrows that were always built. dna.was: zero exports and an apply_grid_config() whose body was `pass`. The acceleration was welded to one binding in _physics_process - read the arrow, apply it as a constant central force, forever - and all three arrows were welded visible. The @identity's own triggers line already named the alternatives ('a constant acceleration bends the path into a parabola; a centre-pointing one curls it into an orbit; zero acceleration straightens the trail into a line') and no map could ask for any of them
dna.shared_with: VectorAddition / VectorSubtraction / VectorCrossProduct are the promoted siblings in this sequence, but the vocabulary is deliberately NOT shared: those benches argue about a construction drawn on static operands, while this one argues about a law of motion. Borrowing `construction` here would have claimed a kinship the code does not have
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03 - the runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. drive is the artifact's own critical_parameter lifted out of the code: central re-aims the arrow at the artifact origin every frame and launches the ball on the circular-orbit tangent, so acceleration changes direction without changing speed; inertial starts from the SAME point at the SAME speed on the SAME tangent and then applies nothing, so circle vs line is a controlled comparison of one variable; resisted subtracts DRAG_K * v so the parabola straightens into terminal velocity, where the net acceleration goes to zero while the driving one does not. The three non-default drives set gravity_scale = 0 (a 9.8 m/s^2 fall is louder than anything they show); constant never touches it. chain is a still-visible axis - arrow count and colour change - and hides only, never frees: under state and path the acceleration arrow is invisible but its grab spheres remain pickable. WARNING for the next editor: apply_grid_config() must NOT chain to super here. This class builds inline in _ready() instead of overriding build_scene(), so the base rebuild() would free every child and then call an empty build_scene, leaving nothing.

The @identity essence line already read `impact -> destroy(method)` and the description already listed eight methods, but the list was not a parameter anywhere - it was the fixed LAYOUT of _spawn_destructibles(), nine unconditional instantiate calls. So the declaration was derived from the layout, which is the only categorical thing this file owns; there is no dispatch table here to read, and saying so is part of the finding.
dna.note: THE AXIS IS THE SPECIMENS, NOT THE BREAKING, and that is deliberate. Every destruction path in the eight destructible scripts is a body-entered handler that spawns RigidBody3D fragments with impulses and schedules them to fade and free; a still of any of it is an arbitrary instant of a physics run, and a still taken later is an empty floor. Pre-breaking them at build time would be five new static-aftermath renderers written across five files that other tokens also place - inventing artifacts, not promoting one. What a still does carry is the built form, which is what the truth line is about: 'how something breaks reveals how it was built'. KNOWN LIMITATION, not a defect to fix silently: a pinned method leaves its specimen at its bench coordinate (the prism window is 7.5 m along +z from the token's origin), because recentring would make `all` and `prism` disagree about where the prism is - a second, undeclared change riding along on the first. A map that wants a lone specimen should offset the token. TWO PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS FOUND WHILE READING, both left alone: (1) _setup_environment() is never called - every other scene in the vectors family calls it from its own _ready, this one does not, so the create_axes(2.0) and create_floor(15.0) in it are dead and the bench ships with no floor and no axes. It also means the framing is NOT dominated by a 15 m plane, which is why no `framing` hint is set here. (2) apply_grid_config overrides the base's without calling super, so scale_multiplier and laser_endpoints have never reached this token; that was preserved rather than repaired, because the curation bay that places it could be passing scale_multiplier and a bench that has never rescaled would suddenly rescale.

dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. The value list is the one distinction in this material a STILL can carry, and it took reading all five destructibles to find it. planar, octree and CSG each build ONE frozen body at level 0 and compute their parts at impact - intact, they are three smooth unbroken surfaces. sectored ships as 8 wedges and segmented as 48 tiles with a 0.01 gap between them - intact, they are nothing but seams. So `computed` is a bench with no seam in the frame and `latent` is a bench that is all seam, and the axis draws the line between a part that is CALCULATED and a part that was always there. That line is the artifact's own truth statement (each method is a decomposition basis) made visible instead of asserted.
dna.declined: an `exploded` axis (whole | exploded) was designed and refused, and the reason is worth keeping because the obvious reading of this artifact demands it: fracture is an event, so the aftermath is what a still wants. It cannot be had honestly. Firing the real path means calling each destructible's _shatter_all_* , which unfreezes every piece (freeze = false, gravity_scale = 1.0) and applies impulses - by the rig's 1.1 s settle the bench is a pile on the floor, and the impulses are not seeded, so five variants would be five different piles and any bite report would be measuring the physics engine. Faking it - offsetting each frozen piece radially by its own mesh-AABB centre, which is deterministic and needs no impulse - works beautifully on sectored and segmented and does NOTHING on the other three, because they have exactly one piece until they are hit. An axis that is a null cell for 60% of the bench is a finished-looking experiment about the 40%. A `grain` axis over the five bases' fineness (max_split_levels 3, max_subdivision_levels 2, initial_sectors 8, latitude x longitude 6 x 8) was refused for the mirror reason: it is visible in a still on sectored and segmented and invisible on the three that only subdivide after impact.
dna.harness_note: framing 0.7 is declared because this subject is WIDE and SPARSE and the axis lives in the sparse part. The bench spans 6.6 m of x with five 0.6 m spheres in it, the throw balls hang 3 m in front at z = 0.5, and the instruction wall is a nine-line Label3D at y = 2.3 that is the single largest bright object in the frame and is IDENTICAL in every variant - deliberately so, because rewriting the caption per value would have measured the caption. Fit-by-diagonal on that box puts each sphere at well under 1% of frame, so removing two of them is a change the critic would read as decoration even though it is 40% of the bench. The caption stays fixed and the camera comes in instead. If the report is still faint, the next move is a tighter framing and not a bigger axis. SEPARATE FINDING, not repaired here: this token is a full test SCENE - it carries its own DirectionalLight3D, WorldEnvironment, a stats HUD and a nine-line instruction panel addressed to a player with hands, and it is placed as an artifact in four maps.

dna_declined.not_a_dna_block_on_purpose: artifact_dna_research.py reads bool(entry['dna']) as 'declared', so an empty or axis-less dna block would enter the ledger as a promotion. Same convention as grid3d_force_directed and audio_catalog_tablet.
dna_declined.it_does_build: This is NOT the tile_meander_floor case. Standing alone the scene renders: a 0.024 m orange emissive sphere (point_mesh.gd puts a SphereMesh of radius 0.012 on the MeshInstance3D), a 0.05 m HighlightRing quad, and a constant red gravity arrow - _setup_vectors calls _update_gravity_vector, which sets gravity_arrow.visible = true at boot. So there is a picture. The decline is about what could be said ABOUT that picture.
dna_declined.axis_considered: `foresight` (parabola | apex | landing | none) and `vectors` (sum | components | velocity | gravity) - catapult's two words, reused character for character by force_pad and human_catapult. They are the RIGHT words for this machine: force_pad's own note says the pad and the catapult are 'the same machine at two scales - both hand a body a velocity and let gravity have it back', and throw_ball is that machine at a third scale, the one you throw with your hand.
dna_declined.reason: BOTH WORDS REQUIRE THE MACHINE TO KNOW ITS OWN LAUNCH VECTOR BEFORE IT FIRES, and throw_ball is the one member of that family that does not. catapult carries default_angle_deg 50.0 and default_force 9.0; force_pad carries forward_force and up_force; this ball's velocity is MEASURED, in _track_velocity, as (current_pos - oldest_pos) / time_diff over a five-sample history that _on_picked_up clears - so with no hand on it the value is exactly Vector3.ZERO and there is no heading anywhere in the file. At rest _update_velocity_vector returns on `speed < 0.01` and hides the arrow, so `sum`, `components` and `velocity` would render three identical frames, and `parabola`, `apex` and `landing` would each need a direction and a speed invented for them. That is folding_past's refusal - taking a word without its answers - and here it would be worse than a dead axis: the tile would be a picture of an event this artifact has never had. The only non-degenerate arc a still could honestly draw is the one for zero initial velocity, which is a vertical line, and under it parabola, apex and landing collapse into the same segment.
dna_declined.the_exports: Ten, and not one categorical among them: velocity_samples is a sample count, velocity_multiplier and max_throw_speed are gains on a rate, velocity_vector_scale is a length, ball_mass is physics, enable_gravity_on_throw / show_velocity_vector / show_gravity_vector are flags, and ball_color / velocity_color / gravity_color are colours. Everything this artifact decides that is not a colour happens between the moment a hand closes on it and the moment it lands, which is the interval a single still cannot hold.
dna_declined.measurement: Computed at capture_config_sweep's own numbers (RES 760, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, radius = aabb.size.length() * 0.5, camera on the union AABB), not guessed. The subtree AABB is about 1.05 m tall and 0.05 m wide, so the camera sits 3.11 m out and the frame spans 1.90 m across 760 px - 400 px per metre. The BALL, which is the artifact, renders 9.6 px across: 72 px of 577,600, or 0.012% of frame, against the ~6% floor below which the brief says the number is a fact about the bench. The gravity arrow adds about 0.15%. A sweep here would run green and report whatever it reported about a nine-pixel dot.
dna_declined.underlying_finding: THE AABB IS SET BY AN ARROW THAT IS NEVER VISIBLE. _create_vector_arrow builds the velocity shaft as a CylinderMesh of height 1.0 (scaled only later, inside _update_velocity_vector, which is reached only while the ball is held) and then sets arrow.visible = false. capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb and GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb both count MeshInstance3D regardless of visibility, so a hidden 1 m cylinder decides both the sweep framing and the auto-ground lift of a 24 mm ball. This is the documented `layers = 0` case in reverse, and it is worth fixing on its own account - it would also shift the grounding of the 3 placements (ForcesArena, Forces_Destruct, Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text), so it is a repair to make deliberately and not a side effect of a promotion. SECOND, smaller: the red 9.8 arrow is drawn while _setup_throwing_physics holds gravity_scale = 0.0 and freeze = true, so the object advertises a force that is switched off until a hand lets go.
dna_declined.what_would_change_this: Give the ball a nominal throw it owns - a declared aim plus the max_throw_speed it already carries - and `foresight` becomes available honestly, exactly as it is on the catapult. That is authoring a new claim about the artifact rather than lifting a hidden parameter out of it, so it belongs to a design decision and not to this pass. It would also need the hidden-arrow AABB fixed first, or the arc would be drawn at a scale nothing can photograph.

dna.default: workings=trace, pair=oblique - trace is the fall-through arm of a match that sits at the very END of _update_vectors(), after the formula panel is written; it restores every layer to 1 and builds nothing, so the five shipped arrows, both parallelogram ghosts, the three vector labels, the exhibition plate, the side formula panel and the VR preset rack are the lineage byte for byte. The only node added to the tree at the default is one empty Node3D holder called Workings, created LAST in _ready so nothing above it changes index or position. pair=oblique SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first line of _paired_b() and hands back vector_b itself rather than re-deriving it from an angle, so `vector_b = _paired_b()` in _ready is a self-assignment and a map that overrides vector_b alone still gets exactly the vector it asked for. All 3 direct placements (Corridor_VectorFoundations, VectorAddition, Vectors_Intro) carry the bare token, as does the curation_station#artifacts reference in Curation_Bay_forces_1, so apply_grid_config never sees either key.
dna.was: four plain exports - max_vector_length, arrow_thickness, vector_a, vector_b - and an apply_grid_config() that was a bare `for key in config_data: set(key, ...)` loop. Sizes and two literal operands were reachable; nothing about what the bench ARGUES was. The parallelogram closure was the only case it could ever make for A + B, hard-coded as two ghost arrows in _create_arrows(), and the angle between the operands - which this file's own @identity names as its critical_parameter, 'parallel vectors add magnitudes; perpendicular vectors add by Pythagoras; opposed vectors cancel' - existed only behind four preset BUTTONS that a still frame can never photograph being pressed.
dna.kin: BOTH words are taken character for character, and from two different siblings, because they are two different questions. workings (outcome | trace | operands | expression) is the shared vector-subject word from transform_composition_workbench, carried by vector_add, vector_sub, dot_aligner, projection_shadow, length_lantern, torque_crank, circle_train and - decisively - by [[vector_subtraction_demo]], which is THIS artifact's twin: the folder next door, the same four exports, the same grab handles, the same four-button preset rack, the same exhibition plate and side formula panel, written as the inverse of this file and naming it in its own @identity. Addition and subtraction living in one directory tree must not draw their workings in two vocabularies. pair (oblique | orthogonal | parallel | opposed) is [[VectorAddition]]'s word, the other bench in this corpus arguing A + B. NOT taken: `construction` (parallelogram | chain | commute | bare), VectorAddition's other half. vector_subtraction_demo already refused it on this same pair of files, correctly - parallelogram/chain/bare are trace/operands/outcome under other names, and declaring both would ship two axes for one question and guarantee a redundant sweep. The two addition benches now share `pair` and the two demo benches share `workings`, which is exactly one word per question across four artifacts.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-06 - the runner refused this artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. pair is the interesting half, because it is the FIX for a decline rather than a new idea: vector_subtraction_demo refused to make an axis of its four preset buttons, on the grounds that a button is a player interaction and a still photographs whichever preset was last pressed, which is never. The question those buttons ask is real; it is only the button that a camera cannot see. pair asks it as the opening STATE instead, resolved before _ready builds a single node, so the handles, the arrows, the ghosts, the labels and every printed component all come from one pair of operands. The magnitude of B is held at its shipped 0.7 across all four values, so what moves in the frame is the ANGLE and nothing else - a longer arrow would be a size change, not a different argument. The values are all real for ADDITION, which is not true of every operation: at `parallel` the figure collapses onto the line and the magnitudes simply add (the triangle inequality at its equality case), at `opposed` the green resultant shrinks to 0.154 against operands of 0.854 and 0.7, addition visibly doing the work of subtraction, and at `orthogonal` the parallelogram is a rectangle whose diagonal is Pythagoras. The axes compose: at (operands, parallel) the dashed sides and the three marker dots all fall on one line, which is the degenerate parallelogram drawn as a degenerate parallelogram rather than simply missing.
dna.still_note: The five arrows are the only saturated things in the frame and `outcome` takes four of them out, so workings should measure wholesale. pair is the thinner axis and will be thinnest at workings=outcome, where only the single green arrow is left to move; expect it to read strongest at workings=trace and workings=operands, where the whole figure re-forms. No capture was run in this pass. framing is deliberately NOT declared: the ground plane this bench builds is max_vector_length * 2.5 = 3.0 m square and the exhibition plate and preset rack stand at z = 1.5 and 1.65, so the union AABB is roughly 3.0 x 1.1 x 3.3 and the arrows occupy about a third of it - comfortably above the ~6% floor, and a crop would start clipping the rack and the plate. For the same reason the `expression` board was placed BEHIND the figure at z = -(max_vector_length + 0.15) and only 0.55 m up, inside the ground's own footprint and below the arrows' own height, rather than overhead like the subtraction twin's board: overhead would have pushed the Y extent from ~1.1 to ~2.0 and pulled the fixed sweep camera back on EVERY variant, including the ones the board does not appear in.
dna.declines: max_vector_length, arrow_thickness, vector_a and vector_b stay plain exports - a longer arrow is a size, not an argument. The four colour vars were not promoted to exports at all: a different green is a palette change. An axis over the ghost arrows alone (drawn / not drawn) was considered and refused as a strictly weaker restatement of what workings already answers.
dna.latent_reported_not_fixed: vector_a and vector_b have never actually been settable from a map, and that is a bug older than this promotion. apply_grid_config's generic set() loop writes the property, but _process runs `if _handle_b.position != vector_b: vector_b = _handle_b.position` every frame, and the config path never moved the handle - so the grab sphere drags the shipped operand straight back on the next frame and the override silently evaporates. The registry has advertised vector_a and vector_b under `parameters` the whole time. It is inert in practice, because all 3 placements are bare tokens, and it is left alone here rather than folded into a DNA pass: the fix is two lines in apply_grid_config (carry the handles with the vectors, exactly as _apply_preset and set_vectors already do) and it belongs in its own change. The `pair` path added by this promotion does move _handle_b, so the axis itself is not affected by the bug it sits next to.

dna.default: workings=trace, order=a_minus_b - trace returns on the first line of _apply_workings and builds nothing, so the five shipped arrows, their labels, the title and formula panels and the VR control rack are the lineage byte for byte; a_minus_b sets _ord_head=vector_a and _ord_tail=vector_b, which makes `-_ord_tail` and `_ord_head - _ord_tail` the literal `-vector_b` and `vector_a - vector_b` the function was written with, makes _head_symbol/_tail_symbol return "A"/"B" so every label and formula line reassembles character for character, and leaves the Order holder empty. All 4 placements (Corridor_VectorFoundations, VFM_01_Foundations, VectorSubtraction, Vectors_Intro) are BARE tokens passing no config key at all, so nothing standing can move either way.
dna.was: workings was already written and working in the file and was NEVER DECLARED - a rescued-batch artifact whose axis existed in code, could be reached by a map token, and was invisible to the sweep, the gallery and the bite report because the registry said nothing about it. This declaration is DERIVED from the @export_enum, not transcribed. order did not exist: `var result = vector_a - vector_b` was welded into _update_vectors and the @identity's own critical_parameter ("the relationship between vector_a and vector_b") was unreachable from any map.
dna.kin: BOTH words are taken character for character, and from two different siblings, because they are two different questions. workings (outcome | trace | operands | expression) is the 15-sibling vector-subject word from transform_composition_workbench, shared with vector_add, vector_sub and length_lantern - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws. order (a_minus_b | b_minus_a | reciprocal) is VectorSubtraction's and example_1_3's - which difference is drawn. Three benches in this corpus argue a - b and they now argue it in one vocabulary; that is the whole point of the word, and a divergence between these three would be a measurement fault, not a design choice. NOT taken: `construction` (bare | flip | chain | parallelogram), the other half of the sibling pair. It asks the same question workings already answers here - flip/chain/parallelogram are outcome/trace/operands under other names - and this file had workings implemented first. Declaring both would have shipped two axes for one question and guaranteed a redundant sweep.
dna.note: order changes what is TRUE in the frame, not just what is shown: b_minus_a negates the other operand, so the ghost arrow, the tip-to-tail leg, the green result and every printed component flip together, and reciprocal draws the counter-difference from the origin so the two arrows stand nose to nose - anti-commutativity as one picture. The two axes compose: at (operands, b_minus_a) the bright arrow runs from A's tip to B's tip instead of B's to A's, which is the same pair of positions read in the opposite direction. DELIBERATELY NOT SWAPPED under b_minus_a: color_neg_b stays blue while its label reads "-A". The ghost colour names the ROLE (the negated operand), not the operand, and swapping it would mean rewriting materials built in _ready for a value the sweep can already tell apart by geometry.
dna.declines: max_vector_length, arrow_thickness, vector_a, vector_b and the five colour exports stay plain exports - a longer arrow or a different red is a size or a palette change, not a different argument. The four preset buttons (ORTHO / SAME / OPPOSE / RESET) were tempting as a `case` axis, and were refused: they are a player INTERACTION, so a still photographs whichever preset was last pressed, which is never - the sweep would have measured four identical frames of the shipped vector_a/vector_b. That is info_board's fault exactly.
dna.still_note: The five arrows are the only saturated things in the frame and outcome takes four of them out, so workings should measure wholesale. order is the thinner one and is thinnest at the default workings: a_minus_b vs b_minus_a moves the green arrow and the ghost pair but keeps A and B themselves fixed, so expect it to read strongest at workings=operands (where a single bright arrow reverses across the whole figure) and weakest at workings=expression (where the board dominates the pixels and only its glyphs change). If order comes back under 1%, check the board is not eating the frame before touching the design.
